definition: The clear liquid that people, animals, and plants need to live.

definition: People connected by being relatives or sharing a close home life.

definition: Someone you like and enjoy spending time with.
sentence: My friend has a red bag.

definition: The place where someone lives.
sentence: There is a small park near our home.

definition: A place where children learn with teachers.
sentence: Our school has a small garden.

definition: Written pages that tell a story or give information, on paper or a screen.
sentence: This book is about a little dog.

definition: To take food into your body through your mouth.
sentence: I eat an apple at break time.

definition: To swallow water or another liquid.
sentence: We drink water after our game.

definition: To make a task or situation easier for someone.
sentence: Can you help me with this box?

definition: To do an activity for fun.
sentence: We play a game in the garden.

definition: To decide which person or thing you want from the options available.
sentence: You can choose a story for us to read.

definition: To complete something you are doing.
sentence: I will finish my drawing after lunch.

definition: To take someone or something with you to the place being discussed.
sentence: Please bring your notebook to the club tomorrow.

definition: To hold or support something while moving it.
sentence: We can carry the long box together.

definition: To do what a set of instructions tells you to do.
sentence: Please follow these steps to make a paper boat.

definition: To make an idea or situation easier to understand.
sentence: Can you explain the rules of this game?

definition: To give something back to its owner or usual place.
sentence: Please return the scissors to the art box.

definition: As much or as many as needed.
sentence: We have enough paper for everyone to make a card.

definition: Earlier than a particular time or event.
sentence: We put our bags away before the lesson starts.

definition: With one another in the same place or activity.
sentence: Our class made a big picture together.

definition: To make a choice after thinking about the possibilities.
sentence: We need to decide which game will work best for a large group.

definition: To offer an idea for someone to consider.
sentence: I suggest meeting in the library because it is quiet.

definition: To examine things to find their similarities and differences.
sentence: We will compare the two stories and discuss their endings.

definition: To make something ready for a future activity or event.
sentence: Our group will prepare a short talk about the garden project.

definition: To make something better or become better.
sentence: Feedback from a partner can help us improve our writing.

definition: To have someone or something as part of a group or whole.
sentence: The new club will include activities for beginners as well as experienced members.

definition: To think that something will probably happen.
sentence: We expect more students to join after they see the club's display.

definition: To act so that something unwanted does not happen.
sentence: We labelled each box to avoid confusion when packing the equipment.

definition: In place of another action or option.
sentence: The field was too wet, so we played a board game instead.

definition: Used to introduce an idea that contrasts with what was just said.
sentence: The room is small; however, it has space for our reading group.

definition: To think carefully about an idea or option before judging it.
sentence: We should consider how the timetable change would affect students who travel by bus.

definition: To judge the quality or value of something using relevant information.
sentence: The team will evaluate the new reading space using both attendance records and student comments.

definition: To give good reasons for a decision, action, or opinion.
sentence: Each group must justify its choice of materials by referring to the design requirements.

definition: To think carefully about an experience and what can be learned from it.
sentence: After the event, we will reflect on what went well and what needs to change.

definition: To accept something as true without having enough evidence to be certain.
sentence: We should not assume that students who missed the meeting are uninterested in the project.

definition: To make it possible for someone to do something.
sentence: Providing school cameras would enable more students to take part in the photography club.

definition: To keep something at a particular level or in a suitable condition.
sentence: The group needs a clear plan to maintain the garden during the school holidays.

definition: To examine things in a way that highlights their differences.
sentence: The report will contrast the organisers' expectations with what visitors actually experienced.

definition: Used to connect two facts that differ in a significant way.
sentence: The first survey reached only club members, whereas the second invited every student to respond.

definition: Without being prevented by the situation mentioned.
sentence: The event attracted many visitors despite the heavy rain.

definition: To recognise a fact or concern and accept that it deserves attention.
sentence: The proposal should acknowledge that wider participation may require more than simply sending another invitation.

definition: To recognise or explain the difference between things that might be confused.
sentence: We need to distinguish a fall in recorded waste from a proven change in eating habits.

definition: To suggest a meaning without stating it directly.
sentence: Calling the room flexible may imply that every activity can take place there, although the timetable says otherwise.

definition: To form a considered judgement about something using suitable evidence or criteria.
sentence: To assess whether the trial succeeded, the team must first agree whose experience its measures should capture.

definition: To work out and explain the meaning of words, actions, or information.
sentence: Readers may interpret the parent's cautious praise as a request for better evidence rather than a rejection of the project.

definition: To make a meaning, distinction, or expectation easier to understand precisely.
sentence: The organisers should clarify whether consultation offers a chance to contribute or a guarantee that every idea will be used.

definition: To improve an idea or method by making careful, specific changes.
sentence: Feedback helped the class refine its question so that the survey measured access rather than enthusiasm alone.

definition: To make a statement less absolute by adding a limit or condition.
sentence: The authors qualify their claim by noting that the results apply only to the students who replied.

definition: Used to introduce something that remains true in spite of a preceding point.
sentence: The trial was too small to settle the question; nevertheless, it revealed a useful direction for further work.

definition: Used to describe what would happen if the preceding condition were not met.
sentence: The review must include informal users; otherwise, a useful space may appear less valuable simply because few people book it.

definition: To present an issue through a particular perspective that shapes how it is understood.
sentence: To frame the debate solely as a choice between speed and fairness is to overlook improvements that might serve both.

definition: To provide sufficient grounds for a particular conclusion or response.
sentence: The uneven results warrant closer investigation, although they do not by themselves establish that the project has failed.

definition: To reduce the force of a judgement or feeling by balancing it with another consideration.
sentence: The report should temper its optimism with recognition that the apparent improvement may partly reflect a change in measurement.

definition: To accept that an opposing point is valid without necessarily accepting the whole argument.
sentence: We can concede that the slogan attracted attention without accepting that its promise was therefore justified.

definition: To find a way for apparently conflicting ideas or aims to fit together.
sentence: The panel sought to reconcile its wish for clear criteria with the need to recognise leadership that takes less visible forms.

definition: A statement or assumption on which an argument is built.
sentence: The proposal rests on the premise that more bookings indicate greater value, a connection the librarian has good reason to question.

definition: A small but meaningful distinction in an idea, expression, or attitude.
sentence: The revision preserves an essential nuance: incomplete evidence should not be mistaken for proof that nothing has changed.

definition: Dependent on a particular condition or circumstance.
sentence: The committee's support is contingent on continued public access, so approval should not be read as an unconditional endorsement.

definition: Used to introduce a situation or relationship that runs in the opposite direction.
sentence: A popular activity may be poorly supported; conversely, a well-supported activity may attract few participants.

definition: Used to present a judgement as reasonably defensible while allowing disagreement.
sentence: The revised invitation is arguably more ambitious because it asks visitors to notice the woodland without promising a particular sighting.
